question: A sum of ₹8000 is lent out in two parts, one at 5% simple interest and the other at 7% simple interest. If the annual interest is ₹500, the sum lent at 7% is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the entire ₹8000 was lent at the lower rate of 5%, the interest would be 5% of 8000 = ₹400.

The extra interest generated = ₹500 − ₹400 = ₹100.

This extra ₹100 is solely due to the additional 2% (7% − 5%) interest on the second part.

⇒ 2% of the sum lent at 7% = ₹100

⇒ Sum lent at 7% = ₹100 × (100 ÷ 2) = ₹5000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Principal = ₹8000

Rate 1 = 5% | Rate 2 = 7%

Total Simple Interest = ₹500 | Time = 1 year

**Formula Used:**

Overall Rate of Interest = (Total Interest ÷ Total Principal) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Overall Rate = (500 ÷ 8000) × 100 = 6.25%

Applying the rule of alligation to find the ratio of the invested amounts:

 
• 
• Part 1 5% Part 2 7% Overall Rate 6.25% 0.75 1.25 Ratio = 3 : 5 Total Parts = 8 units → ₹8000 

⇒ Ratio of Sum at 5% to Sum at 7% = (7 − 6.25) : (6.25 − 5)

⇒ Ratio = 0.75 : 1.25 = 3 : 5

⇒ Total units = 3 + 5 = 8 units

⇒ 8 units = ₹8000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1000

⇒ Sum lent at 7% = 5 units = 5 × 1000 = ₹5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alligation in Interest Problems

When a principal is divided into two parts given at different rates, the alligation method quickly yields the ratio of the principal amounts using the overall effective interest rate.

Shift Method Concept

By assuming the entire amount is lent at the lower interest rate, you calculate a base interest. The difference between the actual interest and this base interest is entirely produced by the extra percentage rate on the second part.

Simple Interest Rule

Unlike Compound Interest, Simple Interest remains constant for every year. It is calculated solely on the original principal using the formula I = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.
